description: The primary accepts every write and ships its change log; replicas apply the log in order and serve reads.

Synchronous waits until a replica has stored the change before confirming a commit (failover to it loses nothing, commits are slower); asynchronous confirms at once (fast, may lose recent writes on failover).
How far a replica is behind the primary; the cause of stale reads right after a write.
The guarantee that users always see their own changes, provided by reading from the primary or from a replica that has caught up.
Two nodes both acting as primary and accepting writes, usually after a failover based on a timeout without fencing.
The field that decides which shard owns a row; it should have many values, spread load and match the main query.
Range keeps key ranges together for scans but creates hotspots on sequential keys; hash spreads writes but scatters range queries.
A query without the shard key, sent to every shard and merged, so it is as slow as the slowest shard.
